text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Next year about one third of Finnish tax-payers will no longer need to file tax returns as authorities will obtain information directly from employers.

- Almost 70 percent of Finns say Finland should stay militarily nonaligned, poll shows. Most Finns accept the eastward enlargement of NATO with little anxiety, with only a third saying it will weaken Finland's security. @
- Declining pulp prices on Asian markets reflected in the weakness of forestry giant UMP-Kymmene's share price, which touched all-time low on Thursday.
- Finland's national ice-hockey team beat Russia 6-1 in friendly international.
- Six thousand candles ushered in Helsinki "light festival" on dark Thursday evening.
- Protection of the golden eagle bears fruit as more of them now breeding in Finland. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- Wholesale and retail group Kesko Oy should make a new proposal soon if it hopes to secure approval of its Tuko merger, European Commission source says, and adds that it may already be too late.
- Plan to build oil pipeline from Russia to Skoldvik refinery in Finland has the support of the World Bank, Neste official says.
- One Finnish brokerage, FSB Pankkiiriliike, already offers share trading via the Internet. Two others, Merita Securities and Opstock, plan to launch web brokerage services next year. @
AAMULEHTI
- Government farm support package cuts milk producers' quotas by about 6 percent.
- Finnish rock band Eppu Normaali touring again after three-year break -- fans in Lahti ecstatic.
- Finnish berry wine no good for communion cup, Tampere dioscese priests decide.
DEMARI
- Centre Party was invited to join Sir James Goldsmith's euro-sceptic group in the European Parliament, which would mean shifting its alliance from the liberal group. @
TURUN SANOMAT
- Turku aims to become known as Finland's Christmas city.
- Permission granted for renovation work to begin on childhood home of Finnish Olympic legend Paavo Nurmi.
